kind: Native mechanism diagnostic; not an engine throughput qualification
hypothesis: Linking a 4KiB FRONTIER write to a whole-file DATASYNC request may avoid a userspace handoff. Compare default,COOP_TASKRUN+SINGLE_ISSUER,and SINGLE_ISSUER+DEFER_TASKRUN rings using proper GETEVENTS waits. Current engine already uses COOP+SINGLE for DATA, and synchronous pwrite+fdatasync for FRONTIER.
protocol: Every cycle completes a synchronous O_DIRECT DATA pwrite, then times either synchronous O_DIRECT FRONTIER pwrite+fdatasync, or linked WRITE+FSYNC(DATASYNC) and GETEVENTS waits. Each mode uses identical initialized buffers and file-size allocation. Point prezeros the allocated image before timing; batch keeps unwritten extents. Setup,initialization,readback verification and unlink excluded from cycle timing and included in process audit.
schedule: One warmup per policy/workload, then exactly five rounds with policy order rotated by round and reversed on alternate rounds.30s initial cooldown,10s between commands,no build/profile/test during timing,1Hz competing-process audit. Preserve every observation and stall.
metrics: All-run medians,paired per-round syscall-relative FRONTIER+sync latency,cycle throughput,CPU,p50,p99. Read back every DATA and FRONTIER to verify bytes. Keep kernel setup flags and errors.
decision: Advance linked backend to a Rust engine candidate only if at least one ring mode improves paired median FRONTIER+sync latency by >=3% in both workloads,cycle throughput never loses >5%,and p99 never grows >10%. Failure means no runtime change; native probe cannot qualify an engine change even if successful.
